To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
sonography is a reliable method of detecting locoregional metastases of cutaneous melanomas.
sonography is useful for the evaluation of cutaneous melanomas with locoregional spread and can be used to guide biopsy and surgical resection.

(1) the majority of the patients with cutaneous melanoma have locoregional spread; (2) sonography can be used to identify locoregional lymph node metastases; and (3) sonography is a valuable tool for the assessment of locoregional disease in patients with melanoma.

the use of the sonographic method for the early detection of locoregional spread in cutaneous melanoma.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the findings in this review support the idea of a significant role for ultrasound in the evaluation of the lymph nodes of patients with melanoma.

the sonographic features of locoregional spread in cutaneous melanoma are not well defined.
